title_ar: الدرس الثالث من سلسلة دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية
title_en: The third lesson of the series of lessons of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares
body_ar:
الكاتب : الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو الدرس الثاني من دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية التي ألقاها ودرسها الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو بمركز تكوين العلماء بنواكشوط

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

كان الحديث في الدرس الماضي في أواخره عن موانع الإرث، فمن يذكرنا بها؟

بالنسبة لهذه الموانع التي ذكرناها هي موانع في اصطلاح الفرضيين، وإلا فليس ينطبق عليها تعريف المانع لدى الأصوليين، لأن المانع لدى الأصوليين لا بد فيه من تحقق السبب، والزنا النسب فيه وهو سبب الميراث غير موجود، لأن المعدوم شرعا كالمعدوم حسا..
body_en:
Author: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew. The second lesson of the lessons of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares, delivered and taught by Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Nouakchott.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

The discussion in the last lesson was, towards its end, about the impediments to inheritance. Who will remind us of them?

As for these impediments that we have mentioned, they are impediments in the terminology of the specialists in the inheritance shares; otherwise the definition of an impediment (māniʿ) among the legal theorists does not apply to them — because for the legal theorists an impediment requires that the cause (sabab) be realised, whereas in the case of fornication the lineage, which is the cause of inheritance, is not present, since what is non-existent in the eyes of the Sharia is like what is non-existent in fact..

The lesson numbers in this series should not be used to order the course until the Sheikh's office confirms them.

flags.context: the Sheikh's justification for why fornication is not strictly an impediment
options: what is non-existent in the eyes of the Sharia is like what is non-existent in fact
what the Sharia treats as non-existent is like what does not exist in reality
what is legally void is as though it did not exist at all
flags.note: A legal maxim (qāʿidah). Ḥissan is 'to the senses', i.e. in observable fact, as against sharʿan, 'in the eyes of the law'. Option 2 imports 'void' (bāṭil), which is a different technical term and would breach the glossary's ruling on bāṭil.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off mid-argument and the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

The argument here is a characteristic usuli one and has been preserved as a reasoning chain rather than compressed: the specialists in inheritance call fornication an 'impediment', but on the legal theorists' definition an impediment presupposes that the cause of the ruling is present and only blocked, whereas here the cause — lineage — never arises at all.

'The specialists in the inheritance shares' renders al-farḍiyyūn, the jurists of the farāʾiḍ, as distinct from al-uṣūliyyūn, the legal theorists. The contrast between the two groups' usage is the whole point of the passage and must remain visible.
The lesson opens with a question put to the class ('Who will remind us of them?'). It is part of the spoken transcript and has been kept.
